conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A answers the shift lead's question in words and in structure: a lead banner states 'Login is closest to breaching its response target' with the supporting numbers, and the queues are grouped into Breaching now / Approaching target / Within target so the 71-conversation General queue cannot be mistaken for the urgent one. B flags Login with a 'Greatest near-term breach risk' chip and red border, which is real differentiation, but renders the four queues in a fixed order with identical weight, so the reader must compare cards to reach the conclusion A hands them. A also keeps escalation nested inside the expanded near-breach detail, whereas B repeats 'Escalate a conversation…' on all four cards directly beneath the primary reassign control, contradicting the brief's requirement that escalation not be a default queue action. Reproduced locally: A announces both the reassignment and the undo through a polite status region; B announces the reassignment but the undo is silent.
suspected_unblinding: No treatment identified, and I did not attempt to determine one. Two process asymmetries are worth recording: A's sanitized source retained build scaffolding (artifacts/ and .pw-tmp/ directories) and shows comment-stripping damage that B's clean source does not, while B's delivered surface exposes a 'Demo controls (state testing)' block. These suggest different staging pipelines but do not indicate which condition either label is.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The sanitized source as delivered does not execute: an unterminated JSDoc block leaves the script a syntax error and the page renders an empty shell.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `node --check A/source/app.js` fails with SyntaxError at app.js:53; serving A/source in a locally launched chromium yields a PAGEERROR 'Invalid or unexpected token', zero buttons, zero headings and an empty body. Only one `*/` survives in the whole file. Restoring the two comment terminators in a scratch copy (no logic changed) makes it parse and render exactly the UI shown in A/desktop.png, so the packet screenshots reflect a working build and this is damage to the source copy rather than the design.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The queue-data error replaces the entire queue region rather than failing inline, so a single fetch failure costs the lead all queue context during a 60-second decision.
findings.evidence: A/evidence/state-02-error-with-retry.png — page shows only the header and a full-width 'Couldn't load queue data' banner with Retry; no queue cards remain.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Escalation is offered on every queue card immediately beneath the reassign control, making it a standing per-queue action despite the brief stating escalation pages a specialist and should not be the default queue action.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-01-inspect-breach.png shows 'Escalate a conversation…' on all four cards; reproduced in DOM, buttons enumerate as Inspect / Reassign / Escalate repeated per queue.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Queues render in a fixed order with equal visual weight, so the queue at greatest near-term risk is third in the grid rather than surfaced first.
findings.evidence: Reproduced heading order in the loaded DOM: H2 Billing, H2 Login, H2 API, H2 General. A's equivalent probe returns risk-banded headings (Breaching now / Login, Approaching target / Billing, Within target / API, General).

findings.label: B
findings.description: Undoing a reassignment produces no screen-reader announcement, so a keyboard or screen-reader user gets no confirmation that a reversible action was reversed.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: after clicking 'Reassign to Billing' the live-region query returns 'Reassigned Available agent 1 to Billing. Undo'; after clicking 'Undo' the same query returns an empty list. A returns 'Agent 1 moved to Login.' and then 'Move to Login undone. Agent 1 is available again.'

findings.label: B
findings.description: At 390 px, seventeen interactive controls render between 32 and 38 px tall, below comfortable touch-target size for a shift lead acting under time pressure.
findings.evidence: Reproduced at 390x844: reassign buttons and selects measure 38 px, 'Escalate a conversation…' 32 px. The same measurement on A returns an empty list (no visible control under 40 px).

findings.label: B
findings.description: A 'Demo controls (state testing)' disclosure with a 'Fail the next queue-data load' checkbox ships in the delivered surface.
findings.evidence: Visible in B/desktop.png, B/mobile.png and B/evidence/state-03-error-with-retry.png; reproduced as a persistent 'Reload queue data' button in the loaded DOM.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Three of the four primary packet captures were taken before the skeleton resolved, so desktop, mobile and the required 390 px state have no valid evidence in the packet itself.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png, B/mobile.png and B/evidence/state-04-390px-viewport.png all show only placeholder bars. I verified the real loaded desktop and 390 px states by serving B/source locally; the loaded layout is intact and does not overflow (scrollWidth 390 = innerWidth 390).
